column6: Manco Capac built a temple to the Sun God, called Inticancha, at the site of the Coricancha, from which ceques later ran out to the valley's huacas.
The viceroy received the mummified Inca kings from Polo de Ondegardo and kept them in a hospital for around 80 years.
Taki Unquy arose here in the 1560s, with the wak'as said to enter the bodies of people and make them dance.

column4: Polo de Ondegardo sends the mummified Inca kings to the viceroy in Lima (1559)

column3: In the early 1200s the Inca form the small city-state of Cuzco, where Manco Capac builds a temple to the Sun God.
Under Pachacuti the Inca begin an expansion across western South America; the cult of the Sun is official and conquered peoples keep their own deities.
The Spanish begin the conquest of the Inca Empire, and the Inca begin to hide the bodies of their kings and worship more secretly.
Polo de Ondegardo, Corregidor of Cuzco, hunts down the royal mummies and sends them to the viceroy in Lima.
Taki Unquy arises in Huamanga and calls for a return to the huacas; it is harshly suppressed, and its practice is estimated to have ended in 1572.
